Name: Hesper_Intro
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: Two hundred and twelve years since the Hand lifted, and I am still the one trimming the wick. Wick! Up. The lamp's sulking again.

Name: Hesper_Intro2
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: Paint's flaking down in the Hem. She wants oil, and she wants it before full dark. You know the trade. Harvest, grind, light.

Name: Hesper_Task
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: Four flakes of Hide Ochre off the Sunward Terraces, up the ramp. A measure of linseed from the flax press. Bartram's slab does the rest. Then pour it in before she gutters.

Name: Hesper_TaskSilent
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: Eleven years and you still do that. Ochre from the Sunward Terraces, four flakes. Linseed from the press. Bartram's slab. Then the lamp. Go on.

Name: Hesper_Waiting
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: Ochre, linseed, slab, lamp. In that order. I'm counting fingers of oil here.

Name: Hesper_RestFirst
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: She's burning clean. Sit by her a while. Let the Ochre dry on you and take some of it in. A Limner who won't rest is just a walking spill.

Name: Hesper_Lantern
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: There. Steady as she's been all year. Here. Take it.

Name: Hesper_Lantern2
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: It's not new. Don't look at it like that. The glass is new.

Name: Hesper_Lantern_Whose
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: A Limner's first one. Cracked it the week she got it. I put new glass in. You can see where. Good. You're meant to.

Name: Hesper_Lantern_Thanks
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: Don't thank me. Keep it lit. It burns down one side. Leave it be, it always has.

Name: Hesper_Lantern_Silent
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: ...On the left. Yes. Who taught you that? Never mind. I know who didn't.

Name: Hesper_After
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: The ground moved again last night. Don't tell me you didn't feel it. Eleven years it's done that, and every year I tell myself it's the weather.

Choices.Label: You've no mirror in the house.

Name: Bartram_Hello
Speaker: Bartram Sedge
Text: Limner! The slab's free, the muller's clean, and for you the scales are always generous. Don't tell Hesper.

Choices.Label: The black door, top of the Hem.

Name: Bartram_Hem
Speaker: Bartram Sedge
Text: Flaking. My sister's wall came away in my hand like wet bread. More light, that's all it wants. Brighter walls. I've a notion about that, when you've a minute.

Name: Hesper_Topic_Lamp
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: Nobody. Everybody. Every lampstand on every back is built to the one pattern: post, bracket, cage. My mother didn't know whose pattern and nor did hers. You don't ask who thought of a spoon.

Name: Hesper_Topic_Soot
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: Soot, off the inside of the glass. Forty years of it. Best black there is, and it's not for sale. I don't know what it's for. I only know you don't throw away what a lamp's spent itself making.

Name: Hesper_Topic_Mirror
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: Had one. She took it down. Said a Limner can't see their own back and it only made her cross to try. I said nor can anyone, that's what other people are for.

Name: Hesper_Topic_Mirror2
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: Madder, she wore. A red coat. I told her it would show every mark. She said that was the point of a coat.

Name: Bartram_Topic_Jars
Speaker: Bartram Sedge
Text: Thinner. Comes up from the west shore in stone jars, and the jars come back lighter than they went. Takes the colour off anything. A brush, a bench, a thumb. Don't get it on you. I mean that the way I don't mean most things.

Name: Bartram_Topic_Door
Speaker: Bartram Sedge
Text: The black one, top of the Hem? Ansel's work, before he left. It was green. He set it, so it'd never want doing again, and it never has. Went black inside a year. Verdigris does. He said that was the green deciding what it was.

Name: Bartram_Topic_Mud
Speaker: Bartram Sedge
Text: First thing my father taught me and the last thing I'll teach anyone: mix all six and you get mud. Every colour there is, and not one of them left. Keep your jars apart, Limner.

Name: Corin_Hello
Speaker: Corin Half-Seen
Text: Don't walk round me. Please. Everyone walks round me.

Choices.Label: What do you see, when you look at people?

Name: Corin_Front
Speaker: Corin Half-Seen
Text: That's kind. It's not much of a view from the back in any case. Bit of charcoal. A note to self the Hand never came back to.

Name: Corin_Round
Speaker: Corin Half-Seen
Text: There. Now you've seen the bit I haven't.

Name: Corin_See
Speaker: Corin Half-Seen
Text: The drawing, under. Most folk have lines beneath the paint. Under Ilka it's all ruled, would you believe. There was a red lady went down this way once and hers were quick, like handwriting.

Name: Corin_See2
Speaker: Corin Half-Seen
Text: Under you...

Name: Corin_See3
Speaker: Corin Half-Seen
Text: Never mind. Sing you a song? I only know the ends.

Name: Ilka_Hello
Speaker: Ilka Thrum
Text: The village wants a fire. The village always wants a fire. Read the chalk before you fetch me a torch.

Choices.Label: How long has she been cooling?
You talk about her like a cow.

Name: Ilka_Chalk
Speaker: Ilka Thrum
Text: That every well with a tick-bite beside it is open, and every well without one has scabbed shut. Everything that feeds on her keeps her bleeding, and everything alive up here drinks the bleed.

Name: Ilka_Cooling
Speaker: Ilka Thrum
Text: Eleven years. A hair's breadth a season. I thought the instrument was off. It isn't. And it's slow, Limner. Slower than it should be, as if something down there were holding it back.

Name: Ilka_Cow
Speaker: Ilka Thrum
Text: I talk about her like something I've counted. She's had young, you know. You can tell by the hip. More than one. I don't know where they went.

Name: Hesper_Cold1
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: She's shivering. The Matriarch. Something under her ribs is drinking the warmth out of her, and if she wakes cold she'll turn over, and we are on the side she'll turn onto.

Name: Hesper_Cold2
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: Odile went to find out what. Eleven years ago, the night before you walked up out of the Furrow. In a red coat. So. Now it's you.

Name: Hesper_Cold3
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: Down the Furrow to the Rib Gate. Light the lamp there, it'll be out. Then in. Don't be clever. She was clever.

Name: Hesper_ColdWaiting
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: You're still here. The lamp at the Rib Gate won't light itself.

Name: Hesper_Return
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: Did you find her?

Name: Hesper_Return_Flame
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: Eleven years and she never once trimmed it properly. Look at that. Burning all down one side.

Name: Hesper_Return_Flame2
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: There. There you are.

Choices.Label: Pour it into the Lampstand. Let the whole village have her.

Name: Hesper_Return_Keep
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: I'll want a hook for it. By the door, on the left. Go and sit down, Wick. You look like a wall with the paint off.

Name: Hesper_Return_Pour
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: ...Yes. She'd have liked being useful. She'd have said so at length. Stand back, it'll catch.

Name: Hesper_Return_NoFlame
Speaker: Hesper Vane
Text: Was. Yes. All right. Go and sit down, Wick.

Name: Corin_Quest_Ask
Speaker: Corin Half-Seen
Text: Since you've seen it. Would you finish me? It's three measures of anything. I'd be whatever you chose. I've thought about it and I find I don't mind which, which worries me.

Choices.Label: I'll think about what you should be.

Name: Corin_Quest_Yes
Speaker: Corin Half-Seen
Text: Take your time. I've only got the one direction to wait in.

Name: Corin_Quest_Lose
Speaker: Corin Half-Seen
Text: The seeing-under, I expect. You can't see the drawing through paint that's dry. There's a place I'd show you first, if I'm to stay as I am. I can't show you after.

Name: Corin_Quest_Waiting
Speaker: Corin Half-Seen
Text: Walk round, have a proper look, and tell me. Terre Verte, Bone Black, or as I am. My back's just behind me. It always is.

Name: Corin_Warden
Speaker: Corin Half-Seen
Text: Good evening! The moss is doing well. I used to sing something. It doesn't matter. The moss is doing well.

Name: Corin_Gatekeeper
Speaker: Corin Half-Seen
Text: State your business. ...Limner. Pass. I used to know the end of a song. I have the gate now.

Choices.Label: Trade 1 Rib Splinter for 1 Bone Black.

Name: Corin_Unfinished
Speaker: Corin Half-Seen
Text: Still half a man, and glad of it this week. Follow the charcoal dashes behind the big vertebra. Only I can see them, but you'll see where I'm pointing.

Name: Ilka_Quest
Speaker: Ilka Thrum
Text: Three wells in this wood. Go and look at each, read what I've chalked, then find the nest in the Hollow Vertebra and decide. Burn it, and the village sleeps easy and the wells scab. Or dress the wells with Terre Verte and leave the ticks their work.

Name: Ilka_Waiting
Speaker: Ilka Thrum
Text: Wells first. Then the nest. Numbers before fire.

Name: Ilka_Burned
Speaker: Ilka Thrum
Text: Quieter, isn't it. I've written the day in the ledger. I've left the rest of the page for what it costs.

Name: Ilka_Tended
Speaker: Ilka Thrum
Text: Clean wells. I'll trade you, now there's something to trade. Don't thank me. Thank the ticks.

Name: Ilka_Trade
Speaker: Ilka Thrum
Text: One in, two out. Written down. The wells pay better than I do.

Name: Corin_Trade
Speaker: Corin Half-Seen
Text: Bone for bone. That is fair. I am told I used to haggle.

Name: Bartram_Grind_Ask
Speaker: Bartram Sedge
Text: Limner, a notion. The Hem's flaking for want of light, and a white wall throws back what it's given. Ceruse is the whitest thing there is. Three measures would do the first wall, and I'd pay you fair.

Choices.Label: I'll see what I can bring.

Name: Bartram_Grind_Lead
Speaker: Bartram Sedge
Text: It is. I know it is, I grind the stuff. My sister's children sleep against that wall. I've told myself the dark is worse. Most days I believe it. There's a limewash of Ochre would do instead: four measures, half the light, and nobody coughing.

Choices.Label: I'll see what I can bring.

Name: Bartram_Grind_Yes
Speaker: Bartram Sedge
Text: Good. Good! Three Ceruse off the Blotters, or four Ochre if you've gone soft on me. The first wall's by the ramp down into the Hem. I'll meet you at it.

Name: Bartram_Grind_Waiting
Speaker: Bartram Sedge
Text: The wall by the ramp, in the Hem. Three Ceruse or four Ochre. I've the brushes soaking.

Choices.Label: I'll go and look at it.

Name: Bartram_Grind_White
Speaker: Bartram Sedge
Text: Look at it! You could read by that wall. We'll keep the little ones off it. We will. I've said so.

Name: Bartram_Grind_Cream
Speaker: Bartram Sedge
Text: Cream. It's a perfectly good cream. It'll do half the job at twice the labour and nobody will thank you. ...My sister did. Take your flasks.

Name: Lacuna_Hello
Speaker: Lacuna
Text: No face turns to you. There is none: only bare canvas, cross-hatched, where one was. A hand drifts up from somewhere near the left sleeve, and opens.

Name: Lacuna_Water
Speaker: Lacuna
Text: The right hand turns a tap a quarter-turn. Water ticks into the dust. The hand turns it back, exactly as far. Whatever else was rubbed out, this was not.

Name: Lacuna_Face
Speaker: Lacuna
Text: The left hand goes to the place where a face should be and stops a finger's width short of the bare canvas. It stays there. Then it turns, palm up, toward your lantern, and your knife, and waits.

Choices.Label: I could finish it. Give you a face.

Name: Lacuna_Hurt
Speaker: Lacuna
Text: A hand rocks, level, like a small boat: so-so. Then it points down at the taps, which are dripping.

Name: Lacuna_Offer
Speaker: Lacuna
Text: Both hands go still. One rises and touches the cross-hatching, lightly, the way you touch a door before you knock. They are not saying yes. They are not saying no. A finger points at you: Limner. You decide what is finished.

Name: Lacuna_Waiting
Speaker: Lacuna
Text: The hand opens toward the bare place again, and waits. There is no hurry in it. Whenever you are ready. Or not at all.

Choices.Label: (Look at the place where the face was.)

Name: Lacuna_Set
Speaker: Lacuna
Text: They stand very straight. The hands have come home to the sleeves. The face you gave them looks at you, warm and plain and finished, and does not change. The taps are dry.

Name: Lacuna_Open
Speaker: Lacuna
Text: A hand finds yours and closes over it for a moment: cool, a little wet. Then it lets go and drifts back to its work. The taps go on dripping. Nothing here is finished, and nobody minds.
